newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toshiba confident to launch DVD-ROM before end-97.
newsitem.headline: Toshiba confident to launch DVD-ROM before end-97.

text.p: Toshiba Corp president Taizo Nishimuro said on Monday that he was confident that Toshiba will launch a new high-capacity digital video disc read-only memory (DVD-ROM) before the end of 1997.
"We are confident that we will be able to introduce DVD-ROMs this year," he told a group of journalists.
Nishimuro also said Toshiba is aiming to be the third biggest manufacturer in the world personal computer market by the year 2000.
In the third quarter of last year, Toshiba was the fifth biggest global maker of PCs.
The DVD format is expected to eventually replace video movies, compact discs (CDs) and CD-ROMs. A DVD looks like a CD, but can hold seven to 14 times as much data.
Toshiba and Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd launched their DVD players last November.
Sony Corp earlier this month became the last major Japanese manufacturer to launch a DVD system, launching hardware for sale in Japan from March and the United States from April.
